_readme: OWNERSHIP LEDGER for the PHYSICS board-PYQ compilation. Sibling of
cross-chapter-duplicates.json, which does the same job for Maths — kept
separate because the two sources fail in DIFFERENT ways and one _readme
cannot describe both.
25 provenance tags appear under more than one chapter. NOT 22: the source
spells the same sitting `28 OR` and `28 (OR)`, so a tag key that does not
normalise the OR marker silently misses three real pairs.
THE TWO POPULATIONS, and only the first is the Maths case:
pairs     — 14 tags where ONE question was cross-filed under two plausible
chapters. Keep one, drop the other. Same shape as Maths.
compounds — 11 tags where the board's Section-C/D question pairs a THEORY
part with an unrelated NUMERICAL, and the two halves belong to
DIFFERENT chapters. The compiler pasted the whole question into
each chapter it touches, so both copies carry both halves. Each
copy is TRIMMED to its own half (user's call, 2026-09-09).
Keeping one copy whole would silently cost the other chapter its
question; keeping both whole would file an ammeter question
under Oscillations.
Plus 3 SINGLE-COPY compounds that have no second copy to pair with, listed
in `compounds` with one part.
HOW OWNERSHIP WAS DECIDED — from the bank, not from topic feel. Every
ambiguous call was checked against the chapter's EXISTING practice rows and
the DB subtopic axis, and in each case the bank had already answered it:
- 'Soft iron ... core of transformer' — the bank holds a practice row with
the IDENTICAL stem under Magnetic Materials -> Hysteresis.
- Mayer's relation / molar specific heats -> Kinetic Theory. Thermodynamics
has NO specific-heats subtopic at all, so it cannot own them.
- adiabatic -> Thermodynamics (7 practice rows); Bohr orbit -> Structure of
Atoms and Nuclei (3); Bohr magneton -> Magnetic Materials (1);
transformer -> Electromagnetic Induction -> Mutual Inductance (1).
SUBTOPICS ARE NEAREST-FIT WHERE THE AXIS HAS NO HOME, never new (user's
call). Two cases are worth naming because the gap is in the TEXTBOOK, not in
our taxonomy: the Std XII Kinetic Theory chapter has 21 printed sections and
NONE is Newton's law of cooling, yet the board asked it twice (Q.3 Mar 2016,
Q.4.B Mar 2018); and Electromagnetic Induction has no Transformers subtopic
though the board sets one (Q.7 Mar 2016). Each such row records the
compromise in its own `why`.
USETEXT IS A SEPARATE DECISION FROM KEEP, exactly as in the Maths ledger, and
the better transcription is often the copy being DROPPED — the Bohr-magneton
copy we discard is the one that typesets n-th properly.
NET EFFECT: 379 extracted rows - 14 dropped = 365 rows to ingest.

pairs._group: Electromagnetic Induction <-> Magnetic Fields / Magnetic Materials
pairs._finding: Four tags. The compilation cross-files anything involving a coil in a field between EMI and the two magnetism chapters.

items.subtopic: Induced emf in a Stationary Coil
items.why: A coil kept STATIONARY in a uniform field: no flux change, so neither emf nor current. The EMI subtopic names exactly this case; Magnetic Fields has no counterpart.

Magnetic flux linked with a coil. The Magnetic-Fields copy is the ONE row in the corpus whose options are typeset inside a single math zone and so could not be split — dropping it resolves that flag with no hand transcription needed.
Coercivity and retentivity are hysteresis-loop parameters. The bank already holds a practice row with the IDENTICAL stem filed under Magnetic Materials -> Hysteresis, so this is not a judgement call.

The Bohr magneton is the magnetic moment of an orbiting electron; the bank's only 'Bohr magneton' practice row sits in Magnetic Materials. The DROPPED copy is the better text — it typesets \(n^{th}\) where the kept one writes bare 'nth'.

pairs._finding: Four tags, all about gases. The split is decided by the subtopic axis rather than by feel: Thermodynamics has no specific-heats subtopic, Kinetic Theory has no process subtopic.

items.why: Adiabatic compression, pressure ratio from the temperature ratio. Seven practice rows mentioning 'adiabatic' sit in Thermodynamics; none in Kinetic Theory.

items.subtopic: Specific Heat Capacity and Mayer's Relation
items.why: Mayer's relation. Thermodynamics has NO specific-heats subtopic, so it cannot own this; Kinetic Theory names it. Text from the dropped copy, whose sentence ends cleanly.

items.subtopic: Law of Equipartition of Energy and Degrees of Freedom
items.why: Cp/Cv for a molecule with f vibrational modes — equipartition. The dropped copy's option A carries a stray LaTeX thin space.

items.subtopic: Specific Heat Capacity and Mayer's Relation
items.why: Specific heat capacity of water in units of R. Same axis argument as Q.14. The dropped copy's option A again carries a stray thin space.

pairs._group: Wave Optics <-> Superposition / Oscillations / AC Circuits
pairs._finding: Three tags. Two are light questions mis-filed elsewhere; one is a SOUND question mis-filed under Wave Optics, so the direction is not uniform.

items.subtopic: Interference and Young's Double Slit Experiment
items.why: Young's double slit is Wave Optics. The Oscillations copy is a mis-file and carries a transcription slip, opening 'The In Young's double slit experiment'.

SOUND waves reflected at a denser medium — the pi phase change that makes a node. Wave Optics is light, so here the Wave-Optics copy is the mis-file. The bank files an analogous practice row ('a sound wave ... reflected at an obstacle to form a stationary wave') under Superposition -> Stationary Waves.

items.subtopic: Interference and Young's Double Slit Experiment
items.why: Fringe-width derivation from the double-slit geometry, mis-filed under AC Circuits. NOT a compound — a single question with one task.

pairs._group: Plain mis-files into an unrelated chapter
pairs._finding: Three tags where one copy sits in a chapter with no connection to the question at all. Kept for the record because the pattern (a stray paste) is worth recognising.

items.why: Converting a galvanometer to an ammeter and a voltmeter. The Thermodynamics copy is a stray paste and is also the worse text — a unicode ohm sign instead of LaTeX, and '(i)into' glued together.

items.subtopic: Parallel Plate Capacitor with a Dielectric
items.why: Capacitance of an air-filled parallel-plate capacitor, pasted into Rotational Dynamics. Six 'parallel plate capacitor' practice rows sit in Electrostatics. The dropped copy writes the area as a unicode 'cm2'. CORRECTED 2026-09-10: the subtopic originally recorded here was 'Capacitors and Combination of Capacitors', which the bank contradicts. The practice corpus files a plain area-and-separation capacitance calculation under 'Parallel Plate Capacitor with a Dielectric' EVEN WHEN THE MEDIUM IS AIR - including one row with air and the same 6 cm^2 area, and one that is this question with 4 cm^2 / 2 mm - while 'Capacitors and Combination of Capacitors' holds the conceptual rows (isolated capacitor, circular plates). The original value was a secondary call made while adjudicating which CHAPTER this belonged to; the chapter verdict is unaffected.

Period of revolution of the electron in a Bohr orbit — asks only for the period, so it is orbit kinematics rather than magnetism. Three 'Bohr orbit' practice rows sit in Structure of Atoms and Nuclei.

compounds._why: SHM differential-equation theory + an unrelated sonometer numerical. The two copies tag the sitting differently ('28 (OR)' and '28 OR'), which is why the OR marker must be normalised before pairing.

parts.subtopic: Acceleration, Velocity and Displacement in S.H.M.
parts.why: Acceleration, velocity and displacement obtained from the differential equation of linear S.H.M.

parts.why: Potential energy of a particle in S.H.M., and its value at the mean and extreme positions. Split from the Superposition copy: this half is a QUESTION and only that copy prints the question mark, so trimming our own copy would end the stem mid-sentence.
Frequency of a tuning fork from the beats produced when the wire is lengthened by 5%.

NOTE the Current-Electricity copy puts the qualifier '(Two points each)' at the very END, after the SHM half, where it belongs to the FIRST half — so that copy is split from the OSCILLATIONS text, which places it correctly.

parts.why: Labelled diagram of a suspended-coil moving-coil galvanometer. Split from the Thermodynamics copy, whose sentence ends with a full stop where this copy ends with a stray continuation backslash.
Final volume from the work done compressing a gas at constant pressure.

compounds._why: Magnetic moment of a REVOLVING ELECTRON (atomic origin of magnetism) + the magnetic moment of a CURRENT-CARRYING COIL. Both are dipole moments, which is why the compiler cross-filed it, but they are taught in different chapters.

parts.why: Magnetic dipole moment of a revolving electron — the atomic origin of magnetism.

parts.subtopic: Magnetic Dipole Moment and Potential Energy
parts.why: Dipole moment of a 300-turn current-carrying circular coil.

compounds._why: ASYMMETRIC, and the only one of its kind: the compiler ALREADY trimmed the Oscillations copy to its own half, so only the Kinetic-Theory copy still carries both. Oscillations needs no edit.

parts.why: Rate of cooling of a metal sphere. NEAREST FIT, not an exact one: the Std XII Kinetic Theory chapter prints 21 sections and none of them is Newton's law of cooling (it is a Std XI topic), so the board is examining something this textbook does not teach. Filed under emission of heat radiation, which is the physics the law rests on.

compounds._why: Geiger-Marsden + mass defect, then an unrelated photoelectric numerical.

parts.why: The Geiger-Marsden experiment. This half also asks 'What is mass defect?', which belongs to Nuclear Binding Energy — filed on the dominant first task, since a row carries one subtopic.
Threshold and incident frequency from the work function; whether emission occurs.

compounds._why: Transformer theory + an unrelated charged-conductor numerical.

parts.why: Principle, construction and turns ratio of a transformer. NEAREST FIT: Electromagnetic Induction has no Transformers subtopic, and a transformer works by mutual induction — the bank already files a transformer practice row under Mutual Inductance.
Electric intensity just outside a charged conductor and the mechanical force per unit area — both follow from Gauss' law.

compounds._why: Hydrogen energy-level diagram and spectral series, then an unrelated photoelectric numerical.

parts.why: Energy-level diagram for hydrogen and the series with inner orbit numbers 3 and 4. Split from the Dual-Nature copy: this copy separates the two halves with a bare continuation backslash where that one prints a full stop, so trimming our own would end the stem mid-sentence.
Whether the photoelectric effect occurs for potassium and caesium at 5180 angstrom.

parts.why: Temperature of the surroundings from two successive cooling intervals. Same nearest-fit reasoning as Q.3 March 2016 — the chapter does not teach Newton's law of cooling.

Mechanical Properties of SOLIDS is a Std XI chapter and is not one of this exam's 16 Class-12 chapters, so that half has no home and is dropped rather than mis-filed under Superposition.

expectedCounts._note: Rows expected per chapter AFTER the drops (trims do not change counts). A commit that disagrees with these is a bug in the parser or the ledger, not a surprise — check before shipping. CORRECTED 2026-09-10: semiconductors-12-pyq 15 -> 16 (and TOTAL +1). The original 15 was measured from an extraction that had LOST a question: the compilation typed item 15's number inside an OMML equation, so pandoc emitted the line starting with '$', the ITEM rule never saw an item start, and board question Q.1(iii) February 2023 was absorbed into item 14's stem. Repaired via defects.json -> itemNumberSwallowed.
